templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The government has decided to make primary education free and compulsory for all children up to the age of 14.'
Assumption I: Many children in the age group do not attend school.
Assumption II: Free education will lead to higher enrollment.
Assumption III: Making it compulsory will ensure attendance.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: All three are implicit. The policy assumes low enrollment (I) motivating the action, that free education boosts enrollment (II) and compulsion ensures attendance (III). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Despite repeated warnings, the employee continues to come late.'
Assumption I: Warnings were given to the employee.
Assumption II: The employee is aware of the warnings.
Assumption III: Warnings are an effective deterrent.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I is explicitly stated (not an assumption). II is implicit — the word 'repeated warnings' implies the employee knows. III is NOT implicit — the statement actually contradicts III (warnings didn't work). Only II is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Use Brand X toothpaste for whiter teeth and fresh breath — recommended by dentists.'
Assumption I: People desire whiter teeth and fresh breath.
Assumption II: Dentists' recommendations influence consumer choices.
Assumption III: Brand X is the only toothpaste recommended by dentists.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: People desiring whiter teeth (I) and dentist recommendations influencing buyers (II) are both implicit. III (only brand) is not assumed — the ad says 'recommended by dentists', not 'only brand'. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The company has announced a 20% salary hike for all employees.'
Assumption I: Employees are dissatisfied with the current salary.
Assumption II: The company can afford the salary hike.
Assumption III: A salary hike will improve employee performance.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: The company affording the hike (II) is implicit — they wouldn't announce it otherwise. III (improved performance) is a likely implicit reason. I (dissatisfaction) is possible but not necessarily assumed — hike could be routine. II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'India should ban the export of food grains to meet domestic demand.'
Assumption I: India currently exports food grains.
Assumption II: Domestic demand for food grains is not fully met.
Assumption III: Banning export will solve the food shortage.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: All three are implicit. Export is happening (I) — reason for suggesting a ban. Domestic demand not met (II) — motivation for the suggestion. Ban solving the shortage (III) — the assumed outcome. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The city council has decided to increase property tax to fund new infrastructure projects.'
Assumption I: The current revenue is insufficient for new infrastructure.
Assumption II: Property owners can afford to pay higher taxes.
Assumption III: Infrastructure development is necessary for the city.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Revenue being insufficient (I) motivates the tax increase — implicit. Infrastructure necessity (III) justifies the spending — implicit. Property owners affording it (II) is assumed for the policy to be viable — implicit. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Walk-in interviews will be held next Monday for the post of Data Analyst.'
Assumption I: Some candidates are interested in the job.
Assumption II: Walk-in format is convenient for candidates.
Assumption III: The company needs Data Analysts.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Candidates being interested (I) and the company needing analysts (III) are both implicit — otherwise the announcement is pointless. Walk-in being convenient (II) is not necessarily assumed — it may be chosen for other reasons. I and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Even after completing graduation, many youth remain unemployed in India.'
Assumption I: Graduation does not guarantee employment.
Assumption II: The number of jobs is less than the number of graduates.
Assumption III: Unemployment is a major social problem in India.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I is directly implied by the statement — implicit. II is a possible reason but not directly assumed. III is a broader inference, not assumed in the statement. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'You should consult a doctor before taking any medicine.'
Assumption I: Self-medication can be harmful.
Assumption II: Doctors are available and accessible.
Assumption III: All medicines require a prescription.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Self-medication being harmful (I) is the reason for the advice — implicit. Doctor accessibility (II) is assumed since consulting is advised — implicit. III (all medicines need prescription) is too extreme — not assumed. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'We should develop solar energy to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.'
Assumption I: Solar energy can be developed as an alternative.
Assumption II: Fossil fuels are limited or harmful.
Assumption III: Solar energy is cheaper than fossil fuels.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Solar energy being viable (I) and fossil fuels being problematic (II) are both the basis of the argument — implicit. III (solar being cheaper) is a specific economic claim not assumed. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The police have put up barricades on the main road due to the VIP visit.'
Assumption I: VIP visits require extra security.
Assumption II: Barricades will ensure the VIP's safety.
Assumption III: Normal traffic will be disrupted.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: VIPs needing extra security (I) and barricades ensuring safety (II) are both implicit — they are the reason and expected outcome of the action. III (traffic disruption) is a consequence, not an assumption. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The parents were advised by the school to buy the prescribed textbooks before the new session begins.'
Assumption I: The textbooks are available in the market.
Assumption II: Students need textbooks for studying.
Assumption III: The parents will follow the school's advice.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Availability of books (I) and parents complying (III) are both implicit — the advice is meaningless without them. Textbooks being needed (II) is so basic it is definitely assumed. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The health ministry has launched a campaign to promote organ donation.'
Assumption I: There is a shortage of organs for transplant.
Assumption II: People are hesitant to donate organs.
Assumption III: Organ donation saves lives.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Organ shortage (I) and people's hesitancy (II) motivate the campaign — both implicit. Organ donation saving lives (III) is the basis of the campaign — also implicit. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The bank has introduced mobile banking to make transactions easier for customers.'
Assumption I: Customers find traditional banking difficult or inconvenient.
Assumption II: Customers have mobile phones.
Assumption III: Mobile banking is secure.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Customer inconvenience with traditional banking (I) motivates the change — implicit. Customers having phones (II) is prerequisite for mobile banking to work — implicit. Security (III) is not explicitly assumed from the statement. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'To reduce road accidents, the transport department has made defensive driving course mandatory for all new drivers.'
Assumption I: Road accidents are increasing.
Assumption II: New drivers are more prone to accidents.
Assumption III: Defensive driving courses improve driving skills.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Accidents being a problem (I) is the motivation — implicit. Defensive driving improving skills (III) is the rationale — implicit. II (new drivers more prone) is a possible reason but not necessarily assumed — the course may be for building good habits from start. I and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Do not go outside in summer afternoons without sunscreen and a hat.'
Assumption I: Summer afternoon sun can be harmful.
Assumption II: Sunscreen and hats protect from sun damage.
Assumption III: People often go outside in summer afternoons.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Sun being harmful (I) and protection working (II) are the basis of the advice — both implicit. People going out in summer (III) is implicit because the advice targets them. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Since the last train has left, you should take a taxi to reach the station on time.'
Assumption I: Taxis are available.
Assumption II: The person wants to reach the station.
Assumption III: There is enough time to reach the station by taxi.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: All three are implicit. Taxi availability (I) is necessary for the advice. The person wanting to reach (II) is why the advice is given. Enough time (III) makes the advice actionable. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The judge has given a lenient sentence because the accused is a first-time offender.'
Assumption I: First-time offenders deserve leniency.
Assumption II: The accused committed the offence for the first time.
Assumption III: Leniency may help in rehabilitation.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: II is stated as a fact — not an assumption. I (first-timers deserve leniency) is the judge's implicit belief — implicit. III (leniency aids rehabilitation) is a deeper implicit belief. I and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The company has decided to shift its headquarters from the city to a suburban area.'
Assumption I: The suburban area offers better infrastructure or lower costs.
Assumption II: Employees will relocate or commute to the new location.
Assumption III: The current city location is not optimal for the company.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: The suburban location offering advantages (I) and the current location being suboptimal (III) are both implicit rationale. Employee relocation (II) is a consequence/assumption for operations to continue — also implicit. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Parents should spend quality time with their children to develop strong family bonds.'
Assumption I: Quality time strengthens family relationships.
Assumption II: Strong family bonds are important.
Assumption III: Parents currently don't spend quality time with children.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Quality time strengthening bonds (I) and bonds being important (II) are both implicit — the reason and goal of the advice. III (parents not spending time) is not necessarily assumed — the advice can be general. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The ministry has launched digital literacy programmes in rural areas.'
Assumption I: Rural areas lack digital literacy.
Assumption II: Digital literacy is important for rural development.
Assumption III: Rural residents will participate in the programme.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Rural areas lacking literacy (I) motivates targeting them — implicit. Digital literacy being important for development (II) justifies the programme — implicit. Participation (III) is assumed for the programme to succeed — implicit. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Do not neglect a small wound — even a minor cut can lead to infection if untreated.'
Assumption I: Small wounds are often neglected.
Assumption II: Minor cuts can become serious if untreated.
Assumption III: Treatment prevents infection.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: All three are implicit. People neglecting small wounds (I) is why the warning is given. Minor cuts leading to infection (II) is the risk being highlighted. Treatment preventing infection (III) is the rationale for treating. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The chairman appealed to the workers to maintain discipline and increase productivity.'
Assumption I: Workers can increase productivity if they choose to.
Assumption II: Workers have been undisciplined and unproductive.
Assumption III: Appeals are an effective way to change worker behaviour.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Workers being capable of change (I) and appeals being effective (III) are both implicit. II (workers being undisciplined) is a possible reason for the appeal but may not be assumed — the appeal could be motivational. I and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The fastest way to learn coding is through hands-on projects, not just theory.'
Assumption I: Theory alone is insufficient for learning coding.
Assumption II: People want to learn coding quickly.
Assumption III: Hands-on projects are available to learners.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Theory being insufficient (I) is directly implied by the statement — implicit. Speed of learning being desired (II) is implied by 'fastest' — implicit. Availability of projects (III) is a prerequisite — implicit. All three are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The RBI has raised interest rates to control inflation.'
Assumption I: High interest rates reduce inflation.
Assumption II: Inflation is currently at a high level.
Assumption III: Other methods of controlling inflation have failed.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Interest rates reducing inflation (I) is the mechanism assumed — implicit. High current inflation (II) is the motivation — implicit. III (other methods failing) is not assumed — RBI may use multiple tools simultaneously. I and II are implicit.
